The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

This appeal is filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, (hereinafter referred to as 'MV Act' for brevity) by the appellant-claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 09.02.2016, passed in MVC No.722/2012, on the file of III Additional District & Sessions Judge,
Mandya, sitting at Srirangapatna, (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal' for brevity) seeking enhancement.
Brief facts:
2. On 25.04.2011 at about 6.30 a.m. when appellant -claimant and her father were proceeding in Bullet motor cycle bearing No.CRM-6845 on Mysore-Bangalore main road towards Srirangapatna on the left side of road one car bearing No.KA-53/N-7654 came in a high speed and negligent manner from Mysore side and hit to hind portion of motor cycle, due to which claimant's father fell down along with motor cycle and claimant sustained injury on NC: 2023:KHC:20788 her right leg, right eyebrow and other parts of body.
She was shifted to Government Hospital, Srirangapatna and for further treatment she was shifted to St.Joseph Hospital, Mysore.

3. Hence, a claim petition was filed by the appellant under Section-166 of the M.V.
Act, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in the accident.

The Tribunal on appreciating the materials on record, allowed the petition in part, and awarded compensation of Rs.1,48,000/-, along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

The Tribunal held respondent Nos.1 and 2 therein,
jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

4. Heard arguments of the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondent No.2 - insurance company and perused the materials on record.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the quantum of compensation awarded under various NC: 2023:KHC:20788 heads is on lesser side.
Therefore, seeks for enhancement of the compensation.

6. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the second respondent - insurance company submits that the Tribunal is justified in passing the impugned judgment and award and there is no ground for enhancement.
That the compensation amount as awarded by the Tribunal is sufficient and adequate.

7. The compensation awarded by the Tribunal is as follows:
Pain, Injuries And Suffering Rs. 35,000/-
 Medical Expenses Rs. 10,000/-
 Food, nourishment, attendant Rs. 6,000/-
 and transportation

Future medical expenses Rs. 25,000/-
 Loss of income due to Rs. 72,000/-
 permanent disability  TOTAL Rs. 1,48,000/-
8.

The appellant - claimant was assisting her husband in agriculture work and was earning Rs.6,000/-
NC: 2023:KHC:20788 per month.
The appellant - claimant has sustained commuted fractures of lateral medium of lower 1/4th fibula bone and has undergone operation.

Therefore, considering this,
the amount awarded by the Tribunal under the head 'Injuries, Pain And Suffering' at Rs.35,000/- is just and proper.
9. The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.6,000/- towards 'Food, nourishment, conveyance and attendant Expenses'.

Considering the fact that the appellant was admitted in the hospital as inpatient for five days for undergoing operation and the need of follow-up treatment, the compensation is enhanced to Rs.15,000/-.

10. The Tribunal has erred in not awarding any compensation towards 'Future Medical Expenses'.
PW-3 Doctor has deposed that the appellant has to undergo one more surgery in future for removal of implants.
Therefore, compensation is enhanced to Rs.35,000/-.

11. The Tribunal considering the fact that appellant was assisting her husband in doing agricultural work and NC: 2023:KHC:20788 earning a sum of Rs.6,000/- per month, has taken the notional Smt. sentences.text: 3 income of appellant at Rs.5,000/- per month which is on the lower side.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, which, for the accident of the year 2011, would be Rs.6,500/-.
12.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.72,000/- towards 'Loss of Future Earning Capacity' by taking 8% as functional disability.

Following the principles laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar and Another, reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343,
the functional disability of claimant is assessed at 13% to the whole body.

sentences.text:
13. Since the claimant was aged about 35 years at the time of accident, the appropriate multiplier applicable as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma &
Others.
Vs. Delhi NC: 2023:KHC:20788 Transport Corpn And Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104, is '16'.

sentences.text:
Therefore, the compensation under the head 'Loss Of Future Earning Capacity' is recalculated and quantified as follows:
Rs.6,500/- x 12 x 13/100 x 16 = Rs.1,62,240/-
14.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for a total enhanced compensation, under various heads as follows:
Pain, Injuries And Suffering Rs. 35,000/-
 Food, nourishment, Rs. 15,000/-
 conveyance and attendant  charges

Medical Expenses Rs. 10,000/-
 Loss of future earning Rs. 1,62,240/-
 capacity  Future Medical Expenses Rs. 35,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 2,57,240/-
15.
Therefore, the appellant - claimant is awarded a total compensation of Rs.2,57,240/- as against the compensation awarded by the Tribunal at Rs.1,48,000/-.

Hence, the appellant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.1,09,240/- (Rs.2,57,240 - NC: 2023:KHC:20788 Rs.1,48,000), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till deposit.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i.
The appeal is allowed in part.

ii. The impugned judgment and award dated 09.02.2016, passed in MVC No.722/2012, on the file of III Additional District & Sessions Judge, Mandya, (Sitting at Srirangapatna), is modified to an extent that the appellant is entitled for an additional compensation of Rs.1,09,240/- (Rupees One Lakh Nine Thousand Two Hundred and Forty Only), along with interest at 6% per annum from the date of filing of the petition till deposit in addition to what has been awarded by the Tribunal.
iii. Registry is directed to return the Trial Court Records to the Tribunal, along with certified NC:
2023:KHC:20788 copy of the order passed by this Court forthwith without any delay.
iv. Draw award accordingly.
In view of disposal of appeal, I.A. No.1/2023 does not survive for consideration and accordingly it is disposed of.
